pages.text: Energy Pipes form the grid network, connecting generators, cells and machines into one system that balances power automatically.$(br2)$(bold)Key facts:$(reset)$(li)Adjacent pipes and blocks connect automatically; all connected parts share one grid$(li)A single network supports up to $(bold)1024 pipe segments$(reset)$(li)Connecting a machine makes power flow; multiple machines share the supply on demand$(br2)Every segment supports Normal, Push and Pull modes and one side can be severed; the tool is described on the next page.

The Configurator is the pipe configuration tool:$(li)$(bold)Right-click$(reset) a pipe to cycle Normal → Push → Pull. Normal allows flow in both directions; Push only supplies connected devices; Pull only drains them$(li)$(bold)Sneak + right-click$(reset) a face to sever or restore that side, excluding power from unwanted connections$(br2)An incorrectly configured pipe can be corrected with two clicks; the pipe does not need to be broken.

$(bold)Four transfer-rate tiers per tick:$(reset)$(li)Akaishi Energy Pipe: 50 thousand$(li)Advanced: 500 thousand$(li)Elite: 5 million$(li)Ultimate: 50 million$(br2)Each tier is 10× the previous. A Basic pipe is sufficient for a single Generator Matrix; higher tiers are required for larger grids. $(bold)The pipe must not become the bottleneck.$(reset)

Route the $(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l) output through pipes into $(l:akaishi:energy_cell)Energy Cells$(/l) and on to every machine to complete the grid. For the fundamentals, see $(l:akaishi:energy_basics)Akaishi Energy Basics$(/l).
